Metadata.title: Mithaq | Serious, private marriage introductions
Metadata.description: Mithaq is an Arabic-first, privacy-conscious marriage-introduction network being built for serious adult Libyans in Libya and the diaspora.

Navigation.joinNote: Waitlist registration will open in Milestone 3

Footer.summary: A private, culturally respectful path toward serious marriage introductions for adult Libyans in Libya and around the world.
Footer.stageNote: The public trust website is live in this milestone. Phone verification and waitlist registration are introduced in the next milestone.

Home.title: A more private, respectful way for Libyans to meet for marriage.
Home.intro: Mithaq is being built for adult Libyans who want a serious introduction process—not public dating, endless swiping, or open messages from strangers.
Home.stageNote: Waitlist registration with phone verification opens in Milestone 3.
Home.trustIntro: The product is designed around controlled access, clear expectations, and a path toward family-aware introductions.
Home.privateBody: Mithaq is designed around limited introductions rather than letting strangers browse an open catalogue of people.
Home.photoBody: The private beta is planned to support controlled photo visibility instead of making photographs public by default.
Home.verifiedBody: Phone verification begins with the waitlist. Identity and liveness verification are planned for the closed private beta—not claimed before they exist.
Home.familyBody: The future private beta is designed to let an adult member involve a parent, sibling, guardian, or trusted relative when they choose.
Home.differenceTitle: Designed to reduce noise, not increase engagement time.
Home.differenceBody: Mithaq will avoid public popularity metrics, follower systems, unlimited likes, swipe loops, and open unsolicited messaging. The aim is a deliberate introduction process with fewer, more relevant steps.
Home.womenTitle: Privacy controls should serve the person who needs them most.
Home.womenBody: Women should not need to publish a photograph or phone number to understand the service. The product direction prioritizes controlled introductions, reporting, blocking, and explicit photo-access choices.
Home.diasporaTitle: One Libyan community across many countries.
Home.diasporaBody: Mithaq is intended for Libyans living inside Libya and across the diaspora, with location and relocation preferences handled as private compatibility information rather than public exposure.
Home.finalTitle: Interested in helping shape a more serious introduction network?
Home.finalBody: The next milestone opens a phone-verified waitlist and serious-intention questionnaire. No government ID documents will be collected during the public waitlist stage.

HowItWorks.title: A deliberate path from interest to a serious introduction.
HowItWorks.intro: Mithaq is being designed around clear stages so people keep control over their information and interactions.
HowItWorks.s1Body: Stage A will begin with an 18+ gate, phone verification, and a serious-intention questionnaire. Government ID images are not collected on the public waitlist.
HowItWorks.s2Body: People invited into the future closed beta will be asked to complete the appropriate identity-verification process before receiving member introductions.
HowItWorks.s3Body: The private beta is planned around curated, limited introductions using transparent preferences—not an infinite public directory or swipe feed.
HowItWorks.s4Body: Direct conversation is planned to open only after both people express interest, with reporting and blocking available throughout.
HowItWorks.ctaBody: We will validate trust and network quality before opening the full matchmaking experience.

ForWomen.title: Privacy should not require giving up control.
ForWomen.intro: Mithaq is being designed so women can understand and evaluate the service without making themselves publicly visible.
ForWomen.s1Body: The product direction does not require a profile photo to be displayed publicly. Future photo access is intended to be explicit and controllable.
ForWomen.s2Body: The private beta is planned so conversation begins only after a mutual-interest step rather than allowing unsolicited direct messages.
ForWomen.s3Title: Reporting and blocking are core controls
ForWomen.s3Body: Safety controls are treated as basic product infrastructure, not paid extras. Harassment, impersonation, coercion, and privacy abuse are unacceptable.
ForWomen.s4Body: An adult member may choose to involve a trusted family member later in the process. Family involvement should support the member, not take control of their account.
ForWomen.ctaTitle: Help us validate trust before private beta
ForWomen.ctaBody: The Stage A waitlist will ask about photo privacy, verification willingness, and preferred family involvement so the product can be shaped around real needs.

ForMen.title: Serious intention comes with clear expectations.
ForMen.intro: Mithaq is for adult men prepared to participate respectfully, verify their identity when required, and approach introductions with marriage in mind.
ForMen.s1Body: Profiles and questions are intended to focus on marriage expectations, living plans, children, family involvement, and major compatibility needs—not popularity.
ForMen.s2Body: A person declining an introduction, withholding photo access, or choosing not to move off-platform is exercising a normal product control and must be respected.
ForMen.s3Body: Phone verification begins at the waitlist stage, with stronger identity verification planned before closed-beta introductions.
ForMen.s4Body: Harassment, coercion, repeated contact after a boundary, impersonation, fraud, and deliberately false material information are incompatible with Mithaq.
ForMen.ctaBody: The waitlist will ask directly about marriage timeline, verification willingness, location, and serious preferences.

PrivacySafety.title: Trust must be supported by product controls, not slogans.
PrivacySafety.intro: Mithaq is being built with data minimization, controlled visibility, reporting, and least-privilege access as architectural requirements.
PrivacySafety.s1Title: Private information stays private by default
PrivacySafety.s1Body: Phone numbers, private email addresses, exact addresses, identity documents, and other sensitive information are not intended for public member display.
PrivacySafety.s2Body: Phone verification is not the same as identity verification. Mithaq will label verification levels accurately and will not call someone identity-verified before that process exists.
PrivacySafety.s3Body: Future moderators should only access the information necessary to handle reports, appropriately flagged material, legal obligations, or serious safety escalations, with access audited.
PrivacySafety.s4Body: Core safety controls are planned as free, persistent features. They will not be placed behind a subscription or engagement mechanic.
PrivacySafety.ctaBody: The public waitlist will not collect government ID photographs. It will collect only information needed to validate demand, trust, and viable cohorts.

Diaspora.title: Built for Libyans at home and across the diaspora.
Diaspora.intro: Marriage decisions often cross cities, countries, time zones, and relocation questions. Mithaq is designed to treat those factors as compatibility needs rather than public exposure.
Diaspora.s1Body: Stage A will ask whether someone is in Libya or the diaspora and their current country/city so we can understand whether meaningful two-sided cohorts exist.
Diaspora.s2Body: Willingness to relocate or live in Libya or abroad can be an important compatibility factor and should be expressed deliberately.
Diaspora.s3Body: The interface is Arabic-first and fully RTL while English support is part of the same architecture for diaspora accessibility.
Diaspora.s4Body: Mithaq does not need precise real-time location for its core purpose. Exact home addresses and live location should not be part of public profiles.
Diaspora.ctaTitle: Help us measure real cohort density
Diaspora.ctaBody: Stage A analytics will examine Libya and diaspora participation in aggregate before private-beta matching begins.

Faq.title: Clear answers before you decide to register.
Faq.intro: These answers describe the planned Stage A public waitlist and the direction of the future closed private beta.
Faq.a1: No. Mithaq is being designed for serious marriage introductions, with limited introductions and controlled communication rather than public browsing or entertainment-focused swiping.
Faq.q2: Do I need to publish a photo?
Faq.a2: No public photograph is required in Stage A. The future private beta is planned to support controlled photo-access choices rather than public-by-default photos.
Faq.q3: Will Mithaq collect my ID on the waitlist?
Faq.a3: No. Stage A will ask whether you are willing to complete identity verification later, but government ID images are not collected during the public waitlist.
Faq.a4: Not in the planned private beta. Messaging is intended to begin only after mutual interest.
Faq.a5: No. Family involvement is intended to be optional and controlled by the adult member.
Faq.a6: Mithaq is intended for adult Libyans aged 18 or older, inside Libya and across the diaspora, including never-married, divorced, and widowed adults.
Faq.ctaBody: Review the privacy and safety approach before the phone-verified waitlist opens.

Privacy.title: Collect less. Explain why. Restrict access.
Privacy.intro: This pre-launch policy summary reflects the Stage A product design and is not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific legal review before accepting real registrations.
Privacy.s1Body: The planned waitlist uses phone verification and structured questions about eligibility, location, marriage intentions, privacy preferences, verification willingness, and family involvement. Government ID images are excluded from Stage A.
Privacy.s2Body: Waitlist information should be used to operate the waitlist, understand aggregate demand, evaluate viable cohorts, prevent abuse, and prepare invitations—not for public profiling or advertising resale.
Privacy.s3Body: Application access is designed around authenticated ownership, Row Level Security, server-side authorization, least privilege, and audited privileged access.
Privacy.s4Body: Stage A is planned to support permitted edits, consent withdrawal, and account/data deletion requests. Final retention periods will be documented before launch.
Privacy.ctaTitle: Legal review remains a launch gate
Privacy.ctaBody: The final production privacy notice, processor list, transfer terms, and retention schedule must be approved before real-user launch.

Terms.title: Mithaq is for adults pursuing serious marriage introductions.
Terms.intro: These are product principles for the public-site milestone. Final enforceable terms require legal review before Stage A accepts real users.
Terms.s1Body: Mithaq is intended only for adults aged 18 and older. Underage use is prohibited.
Terms.s2Body: Users must not impersonate others, create deceptive accounts, conceal material identity facts intentionally, or provide fraudulent verification material.
Terms.s3Body: Harassment, threats, coercion, extortion, stalking, doxxing, fraud, and requests for intimate material are incompatible with the service.
Terms.s4Body: Mithaq may restrict, suspend, or remove accounts for safety, fraud, policy, or legal reasons, with an appeal path planned for appropriate cases.
Terms.ctaBody: Read the community and safety principles that will shape private-beta participation.

Community.title: Serious introductions require respectful boundaries.
Community.intro: Mithaq is being designed around consent, honesty, privacy, and the ability to leave an interaction safely.
Community.s1Body: A declined introduction, revoked photo access, block, or decision not to continue must be respected without pressure or repeated contact.
Community.s2Body: Do not distribute another person's photographs, messages, identity details, phone number, location, or family information without authorization.
Community.s3Body: Threats, blackmail, sexual coercion, financial exploitation, requests for intimate material, and attempts to weaponize private information are serious violations.
Community.s4Body: The future private beta will include reporting and blocking at all relevant interaction points, with a documented escalation process for serious safety concerns.
Community.ctaTitle: Safety is not a premium feature
Community.ctaBody: Blocking, reporting, privacy, and essential account-security controls are intended to remain available to every member.

Contact.title: A reachable support path is part of trust.
Contact.intro: Mithaq will publish dedicated support and safety contact details before accepting real waitlist registrations.
Contact.s1Body: A dedicated support address will be published for account and product questions before Stage A launch.
Contact.s2Body: A separately monitored safety channel and escalation procedure will be established before private interactions are enabled.
Contact.s3Body: Users will have an in-product route for consent withdrawal and deletion requests once Stage A registration opens.
Contact.s4Body: We will not publish an invented email address. Contact details will appear here only after the operational inboxes are configured and monitored.
Contact.ctaTitle: Want to understand the product first?
Contact.ctaBody: The FAQ explains the planned waitlist, photo privacy, verification, family involvement, and communication model.

WaitlistPreview.title: The phone-verified waitlist is the next build milestone.
WaitlistPreview.body: This public website explains Mithaq before registration opens. Milestone 3 will add the 18+ gate, phone OTP, serious-intention questionnaire, consent records, waitlist status, referral codes, and deletion request flow.
WaitlistPreview.note: No government ID images will be collected during the public waitlist stage.
